title: Entitlement-gated aggregation proxy for console usage
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Console usage endpoints currently return joined, high-cardinality rollups that are filtered client-side or with brittle SQL predicates. This exposes two issues: 1) queries sometimes leak rows for tenants without explicit entitlements, and 2) precomputed rollups do not reflect per-tenant masking or entitlements leading to either over-broad access or expensive real-time replication.

Goal: Implement an entitlement-gated aggregation proxy layer that enforces RBAC at query time for analytics endpoints and usage views. The proxy will accept high-level aggregation requests (time range, metric, group-by) and emit tenant-scoped rollups after applying entitlement checks, anonymization rules, and cache-aware aggregation. The solution must: 1) avoid full-table per-tenant recompute at query time for common queries, 2) preserve SLOs for console read endpoints (95th < 400ms for small ranges), and 3) ensure auditable permission decisions and minimal blast radius for misconfigurations.

Scope: backend proxy + permission evaluator + small change to pipeline materialized rollups. Not in scope: frontend UI changes (tracked separately), billing chargeback logic, and cross-org aggregation features.
design_notes:
High-level approach: introduce a stateless Aggregation Proxy service in the console backend that performs: (a) entitlement evaluation using the existing Entitlement Service (via token + project id), (b) query rewriting to map requested group-bys to precomputed rollup shards, (c) per-row masking for sensitive identifiers and temporal bucketing for high-cardinality metrics, (d) cache lookup in Redis for common parameterized rollups, and (e) fallback to an on-demand aggregator that merges precomputed shards.

Key design decisions and trade-offs:
- Precompute-and-filter vs runtime-subset: We prefer precomputed shard merging (smaller disk IO, fast unions) instead of full per-tenant materialization. This keeps storage cost moderate but requires careful shard key choices.
- Permission model: Use attribute-based checks (org_id, project_id, entitlement_flags) with an allowlist for privileged roles. Entitlement Service will return a policy token with expiration to avoid repeated policy DB hits.
- Cache semantics: Cache only post-evaluation aggregates keyed by (org_id, metric, groupby_hash, time_range_bucket). Cache TTL short (30s) for freshness; we will support explicit invalidation when rollup pipeline writes back new shards.
- Masking: For tenants marked as "sensitive", mask identifiers and quantize counts for small buckets to avoid re-identification. Masking config stored in Config Service and versioned.

Data pipeline changes: Add a small metadata field to existing hourly rollups to include shard partition fingerprint and a precomputed per-tenant summary when entitlements require. This is limited to tenants with contract-level requirements to avoid explosion of materialized data.
tasks: Proto: implement Aggregation Proxy service skeleton and API contract (POST /v1/usage/aggregate)
Integrate Entitlement Service client and token caching logic
Implement query planner that maps incoming group-bys/time windows to rollup shards
Add Redis cache layer and design key schema; implement invalidation hooks from pipeline
Add masking and quantization hooks configurable per-tenant
Instrument permission decision logging and expose audit events to kafka/topic 'console.audit.rbac'
Add unit/integration tests and an end-to-end test using a replay dataset
Create migration job: append 'shard_fingerprint' to hourly rollups with safe backfill strategy
Performance testing and SLO verification in staging with synthetic load
Docs: PRD + API spec in Confluence and update Console API reference
acceptance_criteria:
- Aggregation Proxy responds to a standard usage aggregation request within 400ms 95th for <7-day window on staging with production-sized dataset.
- Permission decisions are logged for every request and can be queried via audit topic.
- No tenant receives rows that violate their entitlements in replay tests.
- Cache invalidation triggers within 2 seconds of rollup pipeline publish.
- Masking rules applied for tenants with sensitive flag; verified by regression tests.
- Integration tests pass and a rollout plan is recorded in the PRD.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy Aggregation Proxy to staging with a feature flag. 2) Run synthetic traffic against staging and validate SLOs + permission audit logs. 3) Canary deploy to prod in region-us with 5% traffic; monitor latency, cache hit rate, and audit topic. 4) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% over 48 hours if metrics stable. 5) After full rollout, schedule a follow-up to measure cost delta and any missed access issues.

Rollback: disable feature flag to route requests to legacy query path (existing SQL filters). Emergency path: Block all aggregated responses for affected tenants and surface a safe fallback error to the console UI.
metrics: Primary: 95th latency for /v1/usage/aggregate, cache hit rate, permission evaluation latency, audit event emission rate. Secondary: number of RBAC failures, percent of responses with masking applied, change in query cost (tokens/CPU) on DB. Dashboard: console-usage/proxy-overview in Grafana (new panel).
